Senses.Explanation: Literally, 'one who does or makes': a doer of a craft. Across the Chan corpus the word overwhelmingly marks tested competence—an adept, a real hand, or someone accomplished in the role named beside it. It modifies an adept master (作家宗師), an adept battle-general (作家戰將), and an adept Chan guest (作家禪客); an adepts' meeting (作家相見) names a meeting of people credited with that competence, while the doubled exclamation 'a real hand! a real hand!' (作家作家) praises it. The public interview can ask directly, 'What is an adept?' (如何是作家), and a master can dismiss a monk with the negative verdict, 'Not an adept—out!' (不是作家出去). One transmitted exchange applies the same adjective to 'an accomplished poet' (作家詩客). Poet and Chan master are different roles, but the headword contributes the same expert status in each; the corpus does not establish a separate modern 'author' or 'writer' sense.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide expert/adept sense is retained after the item-8 family test. The poet phrase occurs in seven allowlisted files, but all seven transmit the same Dayu Zhi encounter; no productive reversed or related poet family was found. Expert poet (作家詩客), adept master (作家宗師), adept battle-general (作家戰將), and adept Chan guest (作家禪客) are applications of one accomplished-person meaning, not different things. Allowlist count: 2,744 hits in 331 texts. Productive families include adepts' meeting (作家相見), 117; an adept's means (作家手段), 34; doubled praise (作家作家), 22; adept fellow (作家漢), 14; adept eye (作家眼), 10; and adept forge (作家爐韛), 4. The modern default 'author/writer' is unsupported.

Occurrences.Kwic: 這僧不妨是箇作家。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu Keqin's prose commentary (評唱) on the Yunmen case, (碧巖錄) case 15. 'This monk is quite the adept.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 大凡作家宗師。要與人解粘去縛。抽釘拔楔。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu's commentary: 'Generally an adept master unsticks and unbinds people, pulls out nails and draws out wedges.' Defines the role-word (作家宗師).

Occurrences.Kwic: 爾若要作家相見。便與爾作家相見。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu on Changsha/Yangshan: 'If you want an adepts' meeting, I'll give you an adepts' meeting.' The collocation (作家相見).

Occurrences.Kwic: 師乃掩耳而已。居士云。作家作家。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (景德傳燈錄), (石林和尚) section: Layman Pang (龐居士 = Pang Yun) exclaims '(作家作家)!' ('a real hand! a real hand!') in praise of Shilin. Speaker is Pang, verified from the (石林和尚) head + running (居士云).

Occurrences.Kwic: 若是作家戰將。便請單刀直入。更莫如何若何。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Quoted (示眾) of (興化和尚) (Xinghua Cunjiang) inside the (廬州澄心院旻德和尚) section: 'If you are an adept battle-general, come straight in single-blade — no more of your what-ifs.' (作家戰將) = an adept of real skill.

Occurrences.Kwic: 鉗鎚佛祖，必須作家。如何是作家？」師云：「殺人不眨眼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A direct interview asks, ‘To hammer buddhas and patriarchs requires an adept. What is an adept?’ The master answers, ‘One who kills without blinking.’

Occurrences.Kwic: 時有僧出礼拜師云不是作家出去
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A monk comes forward and bows; the master gives the public verdict, ‘Not an adept—out!’

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰。路逢劍客須呈劍。不是詩人不獻詩。曰作家詩客。師曰。一條紅線兩人牽。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: After the visitor says that one presents a sword to a swordsman and a poem only to a poet, Dayu replies, ‘An accomplished poet.’ The phrase applies the same expert adjective outside the Chan-master role.

Senses.Explanation: A colloquial interrogative: “how?”, “in what way?”, or “what about it?” It occurs 25,720 times in the allowlisted corpus. Chan dialogue uses it to demand the next word or act: Baizhang asks how one speaks with throat and lips shut; Shitou asks Yaoshan, after ruling out thus and not-thus, “you—how?” Productive forms press again (又作麼生), ask how someone understands (作麼生會), ask how it should be (合作麼生), or insist “ultimately, how?” (畢竟作麼生). The phrase also asks about another master’s meaning or response. Early and later records preserve three graphic forms meaning “how?” (作勿生, 作摩生, 怎麼生). These are graphic forms of the same interrogative. Its distinctive Chan deployment is the accountable public-interview demand for a response; the entry reports that dialogue role without assigning an intent.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide interrogative sense. The questioned object and answer type vary, but the word does not acquire a different referent. The narrower family phrase “how do you say it?” (作麼生道) remains separate because its final graph means “say” (道).

Occurrences.Kwic: 是爾如今與麼聽法底人作麼生擬修他、證他、莊嚴他？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linji's Record (臨濟慧照禪師語錄): 'this you, right now, the one listening to the teaching just so (與麼)—how (作麼生) would you refine it, verify it, or adorn it?' Here 'how' (作麼生) means 'in what way' and is paired with 'just so' (與麼).

Occurrences.Kwic: 師問溈山。併却咽喉唇吻。作麼生道。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (五燈會元), (百丈懷海) chapter (師 = 百丈懷海; 溈山．五峯．雲巖侍立次). KWIC trimmed to Baizhang's own question (single speaker) — 'shut off throat and lips — how will you speak (作麼生道)?' — the demand-to-utter collocation; Guishan's reply (却請和尚道) follows in the source but is dropped to keep a clean one-speaker attribution.

Occurrences.Kwic: 恁麼不恁麼總不得。子作麼生。師罔措。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (五燈會元), (藥山惟儼) chapter. After the thus/not-thus double bind, Shitou (頭=石頭) throws the challenge at the person: (子作麼生) 'you — what will you do?'; Yaoshan (師) is left at a loss (罔措).

Occurrences.Kwic: 後溈山問仰山：「此二尊宿意作麼生？」仰山云：「和尚作麼生？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (臨濟語錄), (勘辨) (testing) section. Guishan Lingyou probes Yangshan Huiji on an exchange: (此二尊宿意作麼生) 'what was these two elders' meaning?'; Yangshan flips it back (和尚作麼生) 'how about you, master?'. (意作麼生) as a probe of a case.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰。翹足又作麼生。僧無對。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The master presses again and the monk has no response.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰：你作麼生會？僧便喝，師曰：未在。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The master asks how the monk understands it, then appraises the shout.

Occurrences.Kwic: 今朝啟建聖節，合作麼生舉唱？擊拂子
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A formal address uses the normative form “how should it be raised and proclaimed?”

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰：畢竟作麼生？覺以拂子驀口打。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The question “ultimately, how?” receives a blow with the whisk.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：作勿生是？答：亦不作勿生。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Shenhui record preserves an early graphic form meaning “how?” (作勿生).

Occurrences.Kwic: 向上人分上合作摩生？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Zutang ji preserves a graphic form meaning “how?” (作摩生) in a normative construction.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧曰。未審怎麼生下手。師曰。適來幾合喪身失命。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A monk uses a variant meaning “how?” (怎麼生) to ask how to begin; the master answers with a retrospective verdict.

AlternateTargets: what do you make of it?
Senses.Explanation: Literally, “how understand?” In the Chan record it is a recurrent public-interview question put to one monk or to the whole assembly after a saying, action, quotation, or case has been raised. Linji asks how a monk understands the four stated uses of a shout and answers the monk's hesitation with a shout. Wufeng asks “how do you understand it?” (你作麼生會) after an exchange; the monk shouts, and Wufeng says “not yet” (未在) before asking what comes after one shout or two. In a whisk case, a senior asks how the respondent understands Guishan's intention in raising the whisk; the offered account is rejected with “you had better return to Guishan” (且歸溈山去好). Later case commentary likewise says that National Teacher Huizhong and his attendant both still lacked understanding and asks, “how do you understand it now?” (如今作麼生會). The phrase therefore records a demand for an answer that can itself be answered, rejected, or tested in public; the texts do not define it as silent inward comprehension.
Senses.Note: The unstated object is supplied by the immediately preceding saying, action, or case. The graph for “understand” (會) supplies the verb.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曾有僧問溈山。如何是西來意。溈山舉起拂子。上座作麼生會溈山意。曰。借事明心。附物顯理。甘曰。且歸溈山去好。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The raised-whisk case is followed by an explicit demand for the respondent's understanding and rejection of his answer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰：你作麼生會？僧便喝，師曰：未在。僧又喝，師曰：一喝兩喝後作麼生？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: An individual public-interview demand; two shouted replies remain subject to the master's verdict and follow-up.

Occurrences.Kwic: 翠巖芝云：國師與侍者總欠會在，如今作麼生會？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Later case commentary reopens the National Teacher's three calls to his attendant and asks the audience how it understands the case now.

Occurrences.Kwic: 盡十方世界是一顆明珠。汝作麼生會。曰。盡十方世界是一顆明珠。用會作麼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A prior reply is put back to its speaker as the answer to the master's demand.

Occurrences.Kwic: 諸人作麼生會？向這裏辨得，羅紋十字，一任橫行。苟或未然，切忌亂走。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A teaching-seat address asks the whole assembly and immediately distinguishes discerning it from not yet doing so.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一日，龍問：風幡話子作麼生會？師曰：逈無入處，乞師方便。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The question tests a monk on the wind-and-banner saying; the monk openly reports having no entry.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, "how (作麼生) say (道)?" The phrase occurs 3,336 times in 309 allowlisted texts. It is a direct demand for words in the Chan public interview. Baizhang asks Guishan, "with throat and lips shut, how do you say it?" (併却咽喉唇吻，作麼生道); Baizhang then puts the same demand to Wufeng and Yunyan. Records also use it to demand "a phrase not involving the teaching framework" (不涉化門一句), "a phrase not falling into words" (不落言詮), or an answer from the speaker's own breast. In retrospective questions, it asks how another teacher spoke: "how did Jingshan say it to you?" (徑山向汝作麼生道). The grammatical subject changes, but the demand or report remains speech in an accountable encounter.
Senses.Note: This is not private self-inquiry. Even when a formal address supplies its own answer after a pause, the recorded form openly demands that a phrase be said.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師問溈山。併却咽喉唇吻。作麼生道。山曰。却請和尚道。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Baizhang asks Guishan, "with throat and lips shut, how do you say it?" Guishan asks the teacher to say it instead.

Occurrences.Kwic: 百丈問溈山。併却咽喉唇吻。作麼生道溈山云。却請和尚道丈云。我不辭向汝道。恐已後喪我兒孫。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Blue Cliff Record re-presents the Baizhang–Guishan public case and its reply.

Occurrences.Kwic: 不涉化門一句。作麼生道。陣雲橫海上。拔劍攪龍門。下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu demands, "how do you say a phrase not involving the teaching framework?" then supplies a verse and steps down.

Occurrences.Kwic: 朝參暮請，盖是尋常，不落言詮，作麼生道？拈拄杖，云：三世諸佛總在這裏看看
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A formal address asks, "not falling into verbal explanation, how do you say it?" and then takes up the staff and speaks.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰。徑山向汝作麼生道。曰。他道一切總無。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A retrospective interview question: "how did Jingshan say it to you?" The layman reports Jingshan's answer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云我問你苐二句作麼生道進云不會師云灼然灼然
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The teacher asks, "I ask you: how do you say the second phrase?" The interlocutor says, "I do not understand."

Senses.Explanation: Literally ‘divine or forecast’ (卜) + ‘measure or estimate’ (度): to calculate and guess, or speculative reckoning. The compound has 702 occurrences in 206 allowlisted texts. Its recurrent coordinations identify its deployment without supplying a separate theory: ‘thinking and conjectural calculation’ (思量卜度) occurs 25 times in 18 texts; ‘reckoning by affective cognition’ (情識卜度) 10 times in 6; ‘reckoning under the root of thought’ (意根下卜度) 47 times in 33; and ‘weighing and conjectural calculation’ (摶量卜度) 7 times in 3. Dahui's record says, in a list, ‘do not reckon under the root of thought; do not give a phrase; do not remain silent for a long time’ (不得向意根下卜度，不得下語，不得良久). His memorial inscription says, ‘Chan, Chan: do not use thinking and conjectural calculation; it does not concern written words and speech’ (禪禪不用思量卜度，非干文字語言). The Blue Cliff Record asks whether the cited matter can be reckoned by affective cognition (以情識卜度得麼), while a Wudeng huiyuan master says not to conjecture inside cognition, adding that this becomes inverted imagining (莫向意識裏卜度，却成妄想顛倒). Another master answers an appraisal with ‘if you conjecture, you lose body and life’ (卜度則喪身失命). Across these uses the word names the act of reaching a guess by mental estimation; the quoted records themselves state their objections to it.
Senses.Note: All required definition-form searches were negative for a true self-definition. Nine hits for ‘one who conjectures’ (卜度者) use the final graph as a person marker, not as the definition formula ‘as for conjectural calculation.’ The term appears in questions, prohibitions, appraisals, verse, and later addresses. Its literal act and these observed constructions remain stable, so a single corpus-wide sense is used.

Occurrences.Kwic: 不得向意根下卜度。不得下語。不得良久。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui's own record: ‘do not reckon under the root of thought; do not give a phrase; do not remain silent for a long time.’ Direct instruction in a formal address.

Occurrences.Kwic: 禪禪不用思量卜度。非干文字語言。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui's memorial inscription: ‘Chan, Chan: do not use thinking and conjectural calculation; it does not concern written words and speech.’ Inscriptional voice rather than Dahui's directly governed speech, so MasterName is null.

Occurrences.Kwic: 且道。畢竟作麼生辨的。直饒鐵眼銅睛。也摸索不著。到這裏。以情識卜度得麼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff Record prose: ‘say, then: ultimately how is it distinguished? Even with iron eyes and bronze pupils, one cannot feel it out. Here, can it be reckoned by affective cognition?’ Editorial comment, so MasterName is null.

Occurrences.Kwic: 莫向意識裏卜度。却成妄想顛倒。無有出期。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wudeng huiyuan, Fuzhou Baoguo Zhao section: ‘do not conjecture inside cognition; that becomes inverted imagining, with no time of emergence.’ The section master is not linked through the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰。卜度則喪身失命。問。如何是學人自己。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wudeng huiyuan, Xijing Shaoshan Yunmen Daoxin section: the master says, ‘if you conjecture, you lose body and life’; the next question asks, ‘what is the student's own self?’ The section master is not linked through the roster.

Senses.Explanation: The compound occurs 381 times in 145 allowed texts as a verdict on a person, answer, explanation, or speech, and as a verb for making such material up. A late direct naming statement criticizes assigning difficult cases to newcomers without matching the person and the case: after comparing it to fitting a square timber into a round hole and losing people's time, the text says, 'To call it fabricated—is that not fitting?' (謂之杜撰，不亦宜乎). A playful assembly exchange separates the graphs as a surname and personal name: the staff says, 'My surname is Du, given name Zhuan' (姓杜，名撰); asked why it is called 'fabricated,' it answers, 'If the elder did not fabricate, how could he spend all day talking about Zhang and Li?' (長老若不杜撰，如何終日與人說張說李). Dahui uses the word self-deprecatingly when he says, 'I have not read Guo Xiang's explanation or the various commentators' explanations; I only rely on my own fabrication to explain your silence' (我也不曾看郭象解并諸家注解，只據我杜撰說破爾這默然). The stock rebuke 'fabricated elder' (杜撰長老) occurs 68 times in 40 texts, often in the fuller comparison 'fabricated elders are like hemp and millet'—that is, extremely numerous (杜撰長老如麻似粟). 'Fabricated Chan fellow' (杜撰禪和) likewise appears as a verdict on a respondent, while 'fabricated conjectural talk' (杜撰臆說) names speech. These are grammatical deployments of one shared judgment; the texts do not establish a distinct sense from the proper name Du Mo, whose 18 hits refer to a person or to being silent.
Senses.Note: No corpus witness derives the headword from the person Du Mo. Those proper-name and silence occurrences were excluded rather than used to repeat an external etymology. The alternate 'bogus' is reserved for personal epithets such as 'bogus elder' or 'bogus Chan fellow'; 'fabricated' remains the broad target for speech, explanations, and claims.

Occurrences.Kwic: 最悞人者，有初進禪門，根本未悟，遂令參南泉斬猫，百丈野狐，丹霞燒佛，女子出定等話，此真方木逗圓孔，唐喪人光陰，而天地懸隔者矣。謂之杜撰，不亦宜乎？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Sayings on Tempering the Chan Gate, section on selecting material. The author directly applies the name to mismatching a newcomer and the cases assigned.

Occurrences.Kwic: 自云：「姓杜，名撰。」「你如何喚作杜撰？」自云：「被長老帶累。」「長老如何帶累你？」自云：「長老若不杜撰，如何終日與人說張說李？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Tian'an Sheng. A staged dialogue with the staff splits the two graphs as a name and then uses the compound as a verb.

Occurrences.Kwic: 我也不曾看郭象解并諸家注解。只據我杜撰說破爾這默然。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continuation of the Record of the Transmission of the Lamp, Dahui's reply to a scholar. Dahui applies the word to his own explanation.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰不涉程途一句作麼生道。師以坐具摵一摵曰。杜撰長老如麻似粟。拂袖而出。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continuation of the Record of the Transmission of the Lamp, Ju's encounter with Langya. Ju uses the stock 'fabricated elders are like hemp and millet' rebuke; the dialogue remains unkeyed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師嘗勘一新到曰：何方聖者？甚處靈祇？僧曰：臨朕碪。師曰：杜撰禪和，如麻似粟。參堂去！
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Collection of the Five Lamps. A master tests a newcomer and gives the personal verdict 'fabricated Chan fellow'; the two-speaker exchange is unkeyed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 莫是智過佛祖耶？杜撰臆說耶？卓拄杖曰：好向暮天沙上望，西風驚起鴈行斜。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Collection of the Five Lamps. The phrase 'fabricated conjectural talk' applies the headword directly to speech.
